description: baseline: one-forward-per-instance GreaseLM+LoRA, lora_r=64/alpha=128/dropout=0.1 on query,value,key,dense, k=2 cross-modal layers, pos_weight, st3_loss_weight=2.0, lr=2e-4, full train/dev, 10 epochs, batch=16

exp02: exp01 recipe with k 2->3 (more cross-modal GATConvE+MInt layers). Best at epoch10 (0.606), slightly below exp01's 0.614 and noisier epoch-to-epoch (0.461/0.480/0.532/0.544/0.571/0.594/0.600/0.584/0.596/0.606) than exp01's steadier climb. More cross-modal layers does not help here; reverting to k=2 as standing default

exp03: exp01 recipe with max_length 256->384 (more context for the LM). Best at epoch10 (0.610, tied epoch9), slightly below exp01's 0.614. More context doesn't help here (segments/labels already substring-matched on full untruncated text regardless of max_length) and costs more compute (~1.7min/epoch vs exp01's ~1.1min); reverting to max_length=256 as standing default

exp04: exp01 recipe with lora_alpha 128->192 (r=64 unchanged, alpha/r ratio 2.0->3.0). New best, best at epoch8 (mean_macro_f1=0.619 vs exp01's 0.614), st3 notably up (0.554 vs 0.519) and st3_family too (0.617 vs 0.602), st1 down a touch (0.700 vs 0.710). Epochs 8-10 close together (0.619/0.613/0.612), plateaued rather than still climbing. Adopting alpha=192 as new standing default, trying alpha=256 next to see if the pattern from the plain-LoRA sweep (peak near alpha=128, overshoot at 256) also holds here

exp05: exp04 recipe with lora_alpha 192->256 (alpha/r ratio 3.0->4.0). Best at epoch10 (0.615, still climbing: 0.596/0.609/0.615), close to but below exp04's 0.619. st3_family hits a new high (0.632) but st1/st2 both slightly down vs exp04. Confirms alpha=192 is at or near the ceiling of this sweep; reverting to alpha=192 (exp04) as standing default and closing out the alpha sweep

exp06: exp04 recipe (alpha=192) with st3_loss_weight 2.0->3.0. Best at epoch10 (0.598, tied epoch7's 0.598), well below exp04's 0.619 -- st3 continues climbing (0.554, best yet at this alpha) and st3_family hits 0.625 but st1/st2 both drop noticeably (st1 0.658-0.689 vs exp04's 0.660-0.700, st2 0.580 vs 0.605), net loss. Reverting to st3_loss_weight=2.0 (exp04) as standing default

exp07: exp04 recipe (alpha=192) with batch_size 16->8 (more gradient updates per epoch: 294 steps vs 148). New best, best at epoch8 (mean_macro_f1=0.629, st1 spikes to 0.756), above exp04's 0.619. Noisier st1 epoch-to-epoch (0.594/0.599/0.583/0.604/0.585/0.625/0.655/0.756/0.672/0.691) consistent with smaller batch size, but net win. Adopting batch_size=8 as new standing default

exp08: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with bigger GNN capacity: concept_dim 100->128, n_attention_head 2->4, fc_dim 200->300. Broke training: train loss flat ~4.35-4.44 across all 10 epochs (vs exp07's steady 4.11->1.49 decline) and dev metrics cycle between two near-constant values every epoch (st2=0.179 and st3=0.003 literally constant all 10 epochs) -- looks like output collapsed to an input-independent constant rather than a shape bug (isolated 8-example overfit smoke test with the same concept_dim/n_attention_head/fc_dim DID show loss dropping 3.77->2.45 over 5 steps with real LoRA/trunk/head gradients, so the model is not structurally broken). Best guess without deeper investigation (kept brief per budget): scaling the GNN-side width while keeping the shared global grad-clip norm=1.0 across ALL trainable params (LoRA + GNN + trunk + heads together) may starve the LoRA/backbone's effective update size once the larger trunk/pooler/GATConvE contribute more raw gradient mass at full-dataset scale (not visible in a 5-step/8-example smoke test); alternatively a BatchNorm1d running-stats instability inside GATConvE's edge_encoder/mlp at the wider channel count, triggered only by real full-dataset batch diversity. Reverting to exp07's concept_dim=100/n_attention_head=2/fc_dim=200 as standing default; not pursuing GNN-capacity scaling further this session

exp09: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with lr 2e-4->1e-4 (hoping to smooth exp07's noisy epoch-to-epoch st1 swings, e.g. its spike to 0.756 at epoch8). Best at epoch5 (mean_macro_f1=0.588) then plateaus/declines (0.567/0.577/0.563/0.561/0.557) -- clearly below exp07's 0.629 and even below exp01's 0.614. Lower lr just slows convergence within the fixed 10-epoch budget rather than stabilizing it; reverting to lr=2e-4 (exp07) as standing default

exp10: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with lora_dropout 0.1->0.05 (less regularization, hoping to help the already-strong bs=8 recipe converge further). Best at epoch6 (mean_macro_f1=0.606, st1 spikes to 0.735) then wobbles down (0.572/0.599/0.586/0.583), below exp07's 0.629. Less dropout doesn't help at this alpha/batch-size combo; exp07 (dropout=0.1) remains the best recipe found this session. Closing out the 10-iteration budget

exp11: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192, seed=42) rerun with seed=1 to check stability. Best at epoch5 (0.602), below exp07's 0.629 -- a ~0.027 gap purely from seed, confirming this recipe has real epoch-to-epoch/seed-to-seed noise (consistent with the st1 swings already seen at bs=8). Not a hyperparameter change, a variance check; exp07 (seed=42) remains the logged best since that's the actual run recorded, but true expected performance of this recipe is more like 0.60-0.63 than a single point estimate

exp12: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with kg_mode combined->legal (only st3_flag nodes are real in this graph; st1/st2 candidate nodes are all isolated placeholders per _mint_missing_candidate_nodes). Best at epoch10, still climbing (0.606), below exp07's 0.606 combined but closer than expected -- suggests the GNN's contribution on this task leans more on the LM-side substring-heuristic node marking and MInt fusion mechanics than on rich graph connectivity specifically, since even a mostly-isolated-node graph gets most of the way there. Reverting to kg_mode=combined as standing default (still the only KG with real coverage for every label)

exp13: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with kg_mode combined->flow (no st1/st2/st3 label nodes at all in this graph -- every candidate node is an isolated placeholder, only the flow's own reasoning/instrument/outcome nodes are real). Best at epoch10 (0.601), close to legal (0.606) and combined (0.629) but still below both. Confirms kg_mode ranking combined > legal > flow, i.e. richer graph coverage for the actual candidate labels does help somewhat, though the gap is smaller than expected (0.601 vs 0.629, ~0.028) -- most of the mechanism's value seems to come from the substring-heuristic node marking + MInt fusion architecture itself rather than deep graph connectivity. Reverting to kg_mode=combined as standing default, closing out the kg_mode ablation

exp14: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with --no-info-exchange (disables MInt: the GATConvE layer still runs and updates node embeddings that feed graph_vecs/Z_vecs into the trunk, but the bidirectional LM[CLS]<->GNN-context-node fusion mid-network is skipped). Best at epoch9 (0.603), below exp07's 0.629 with info_exchange on (~0.026 gap) -- confirms MInt fusion is doing real, positive work, not just the graph-vecs/Z_vecs pooling alone at the end. Reverting to info_exchange=True (default) as standing default; this ablation is useful evidence the GreaseLM mechanism (not just LoRA) is contributing to the win

exp15: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with k 2->1 (fewer cross-modal GATConvE+MInt layers). Collapsed like exp08: epoch1 shows some signal (0.197) then flatlines near-constant for epochs 2-10 (mean_macro_f1 0.111-0.171, st3 pinned near 0.003-0.05, st2 pinned 0.179-0.187) -- strikingly similar failure signature to exp08's collapse (st3=0.003, st2~0.18) despite k=1 being the OPPOSITE architectural change from exp08's wider-GNN k=2. Since every other run at k=2/concept_dim=100/n_attention_head=2/fc_dim=200 (the validated defaults) trained fine, and BOTH deviations from that combo (wider GNN at k=2, or k=1 at default width) collapsed near-identically, suspect a shared root cause independent of the specific dims -- likely the hardcoded global torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable, 1.0) in greaselm_lora_train.py starving effective gradient budget once the mix of trainable-param gradient magnitudes shifts away from the validated k=2/default-width combo. Investigating with a --clip-norm flag next rather than abandoning k=1/bigger-GNN outright

exp16: exp15 (k=1) rerun with --clip-norm 1.0->5.0 to test the grad-clip-starvation theory. Partial result: train loss now actually decreases (4.35->4.03 over 10 epochs) instead of exp08's completely flat 4.35-4.44, so raising clip norm does unstick SOME learning -- but dev metrics still degenerate near-constant after epoch1 (best=0.260 at epoch1, then flatlines 0.11-0.22) and loss plateaus far above successful runs' ~1.5 floor. Revised theory: k=1 isn't a bug at all, just much slower to converge (only one cross-modal GATConvE+MInt layer, right at the final LM block) and doesn't reach useful predictions within the fixed 10-epoch budget -- clip-norm was partially starving it but even unstarved it's fundamentally weaker at this depth/epoch-budget combo. Not pursuing k=1 further; trying clip-norm=5.0 on exp08's wider-GNN config next since that one was COMPLETELY flat (not just slow), a stronger signal something else is actually broken there

exp17: exp08's bigger-GNN config (concept_dim 100->128, n_attention_head 2->4, fc_dim 200->300) rerun with --clip-norm 1.0->5.0. CONFIRMED the grad-clip-starvation theory: train loss now declines steadily 3.99->1.28 (vs exp08's completely flat 4.35-4.44) and dev metrics recover to a real learning curve, best=0.618 at epoch7. This is close to exp07's 0.629 but doesn't beat it yet -- the wider GNN's extra capacity isn't paying for itself within 10 epochs even when correctly unstuck. Real fix confirmed though: the hardcoded clip_grad_norm_=1.0 was genuinely starving bigger-capacity variants of this model, not a fundamental architecture flaw. Worth trying clip_norm=5.0 on exp07's default-width recipe too (does it help there, or was width the trigger for needing it) and possibly clip_norm=10.0 on this bigger-GNN config to see if it climbs further

exp18: exp17's bigger-GNN config with --clip-norm 5.0->10.0. Best at epoch10 (0.601, tied epoch9), slightly below exp17's clip=5.0 result (0.618). Loss trajectory nearly identical to exp17 (4.03->1.32 vs 4.03->1.28), so 10.0 isn't meaningfully looser than 5.0 in practice here -- clip=5.0 was already past the point where clipping was the bottleneck. Confirms clip_norm=5.0 as the better setting for wider-GNN configs; reverting to that

exp19: exp07's default-width recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with --clip-norm 1.0->5.0, as a control for the exp17/18 finding. Best at epoch7 (0.603), below exp07's 0.629 with clip=1.0 -- confirms clip_norm=1.0 is fine (even slightly better) at default width, and clip=5.0 was specifically needed to unstick the WIDER-GNN configs (exp08/17/18), not a generally-better setting. clip_norm should scale with model capacity, not be raised blindly. Reverting to clip_norm=1.0 (default) for default-width recipes

exp20: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with st3_loss_weight 2.0->1.5 (untested combo -- st3_loss_weight=3.0 was only previously tried at bs=16/alpha=192 in exp06). Best at epoch10 (0.616, close to epoch8's 0.615), close to but below exp07's 0.629 -- st2 hits a new high (0.629) but st1/st3 both slightly down vs exp07. st3_loss_weight=2.0 remains better than both 1.5 and 3.0 at this bs=8/alpha=192 combo; reverting to st3_loss_weight=2.0 as standing default

exp21: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with batch_size 8->4 (testing whether the bs=16->8 trend of 'more updates helps' continues further). Best at epoch8 (0.600), below exp07's 0.629 and even below exp01's 0.614 baseline -- the smaller-batch trend reverses at bs=4, noisier still (st1 swings 0.568/0.479/0.611/0.580/0.683/0.606/0.645/0.687/0.637/0.653) without the corresponding gain. Confirms bs=8 is a genuine sweet spot, not a monotonic 'smaller is better' trend; reverting to batch_size=8 as standing default

exp22: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with --num-unfrozen-lm-layers 2 (new feature: fully fine-tunes the trailing 2 transformer blocks on top of LoRA, ~19% trainable vs exp07's ~8.5%). Best at epoch10, still climbing (0.580), below exp07's 0.629 -- more trainable capacity (full weights, not just LoRA A/B) slows convergence within the fixed 10-epoch budget rather than helping, similar in spirit to the wider-GNN finding (exp08/17) though this one didn't collapse, just underperforms and is still improving at the epoch10 cutoff. Feature confirmed working (verified via standalone gradient check before this run); trying --num-unfrozen-lm-layers 1 next (lighter touch) before abandoning this direction

exp23: exp07 recipe (bs=8, alpha=192) with --num-unfrozen-lm-layers 1 (lighter touch than exp22's 2). Best at epoch8 (0.620), better than exp22's 0.580 (2 layers) but still below exp07's pure-LoRA 0.629. Confirms a monotonic pattern: 0 unfrozen full layers (exp07, LoRA-only) > 1 (exp23) > 2 (exp22) -- adding full-weight fine-tuning capacity on top of LoRA consistently costs convergence speed within the fixed 10-epoch budget here, doesn't help even at the lightest touch. Reverting to num-unfrozen-lm-layers=0 (LoRA-only) as standing default; closing out this direction
